stages.name: Elementary school (K–5)
stages.blurb: Numbers, reading and writing, science and the world around us, plus philosophy for children: wondering together about big questions, asking good questions and giving reasons, with a grown-up close by.

stages.name: Middle school (6–8)
stages.blurb: Ratios to algebra, reading and writing, the sciences and history, plus reasoning well (arguments, evidence and fallacies) and a first course in the big questions of philosophy.

stages.name: High school (9–12)
stages.blurb: Algebra through calculus and statistics, the lab sciences, English and history, plus an introduction to philosophy, logic and critical reasoning, and ethics.

stages.name: College philosophy degree
stages.blurb: The core of a philosophy major with a concentration in metaphysics: symbolic logic and logic with Python, the history of philosophy from the ancient Greeks to the twentieth century, ethics, epistemology, philosophy of mind, language, science, physics and religion, two courses in metaphysics, world philosophies, and intermediate and modal logic.

stages.name: Graduate study and research in metaphysics
stages.blurb: Graduate seminars in contemporary metaphysics, mind and consciousness, and the metaphysics of science and physics, formal methods, philosophical research and writing, and preparation for qualifying exams and a dissertation prospectus.
